title: THING//MANIA hybrid AC-02: THE APPLIANCES TAKE OVER (x4 listening copy)
description: Listening copy of ac-02-appliances-take-over.json: the identical eight-bar loop placed at bars 1, 9, 17 and 25, then one closing downbeat at bar 33 that decays inside that bar. Same tracks, mix and master.

tracks.description: A's squelch bass riff (unchanged sound, same choke and processing).
Parallel high-passed, driven copy of the bass so the riff carries on phone speakers (2 dB hotter than A).
A's whistle: hook, pickups and answers. Panned 0.3 and 1 dB up, which keeps A's level under the balance pan law.
The same whistle without its dotted-eighth echo, for the phrases that hand over to an appliance: the echo would land exactly on the appliance's entry.
Em9 stabs on the swung off-beats; they step aside whenever an appliance sings.
A's kick, locked to the bass on 1 and 3-and.
Parallel crunch bus: the kick and snare hits again, high-passed and driven hard so the kit has bite and reads on phones.
Swung 16ths accenting the off-beat eighths; open hat on 4-and in odd bars, choked by the next closed hat.
The lead appliance (toaster): grabs the hook in bar 3, holds YAAAH in bar 4, chants 2+2+3 twice across bars 5-6, the bent tag in the bar-7 breakdown, and sags with the power failure.
The kettle: parallel fourths under the hook (bar 3) and the breakdown tag (bar 7).
Close-harmony choir: E minor under the bar-4 YAAAH, A major under the bar-6 YAAAH, "da" stabs in place of the clav in bar 7, and the bar-8 slip chord sagging three semitones.
C's cardboard-box kick under A's kick and spoon-on-pot-lid under the backbeat once the appliances arrive (bars 3-6); in the bar-7 breakdown they replace the drum kit.
C's rice-jar shaker opposite the hats from bar 3; it winds down as the power fails.
